sources.title: Edward Witten, Light Rays, Singularities, and All That, Clay Mathematics Institute lecture notes, arXiv:1901.03928v6 (2023)
sources.locator: Read §§5.2 Promptness And Focal Points, 5.3 More On The Boundary Of The Future, 5.4 The Null Raychaudhuri Equation, 5.5 Trapped Surfaces and 5.6 Penrose’s Theorem; §6.2 The Black Hole Region; and Appendix B Two Coordinate Systems For de Sitter Space.

contents.name: §5.2 Promptness And Focal Points
contents.support: Supports the role of focal points in ending a generator’s contribution to the future boundary; the local argument uses the exact focal-exclusion supplier with its continuation hypothesis.

contents.name: §5.3 More On The Boundary Of The Future
contents.support: Supports the horismos and boundary-generator context; the equality with ∂I⁺(S) and its topology are proved from the local causal suppliers.

contents.name: §5.4 The Null Raychaudhuri Equation
contents.support: Supports null focusing; the proof applies the inspected Raychaudhuri proposition under its explicit affine and Ricci hypotheses.

contents.name: §5.5 Trapped Surfaces
contents.support: Supports the two-future-null-expansion convention and contextualizes the exact round-sphere calculation in ex-gr-fx06-1.

contents.name: Minkowski has no compact future trapped surface (the global claim made within §5.5)
contents.reason: The assigned example verifies only the two standard round-sphere expansions. The stronger all-surfaces claim needs a separate application of Penrose’s theorem to Minkowski and is outside this leaf’s planned statement.

contents.name: §5.6 Penrose’s Theorem
contents.support: Supports the theorem’s geometric route and the distinction between affine incompleteness and curvature blow-up; the local theorem and its added slice-transfer lemma are proved in full.

contents.name: §6.2 The Black Hole Region
contents.support: Supports defining the black region and event horizon relative to supplied asymptotic data; the local definition does not assert that such a completion exists.

contents.name: Appendix B Two Coordinate Systems For de Sitter Space
contents.support: Supplies the global hyperboloid and scale-factor coordinate form; the example separately proves the Cauchy, curvature, completeness, and trapping claims for its chosen model.

source_review.read_extent: Read the text of §§5.2–5.6 and §6.2, and the de Sitter coordinate derivation in Appendix B, including the complete Penrose proof route in §5.6.
source_review.supports: Null promptness, trapped-surface definitions, focal-point use, the Penrose topological argument, the asymptotic black-hole region, and global de Sitter coordinates.
source_review.limitations: Witten uses the null energy condition together with Einstein’s equation in the theorem discussion; this batch assumes null Ricci nonnegativity directly. Witten’s de Sitter exercise also studies a contracting subregion with a noncompact Cauchy surface; ex-gr-fx06-2 instead proves claims for the full global de Sitter hyperboloid. The source’s no-trapped-surface statement for all of Minkowski is stronger than the assigned round-sphere calculation and is recorded out of scope.

sources.title: José M. M. Senovilla and David Garfinkle, The 1965 Penrose singularity theorem, Classical and Quantum Gravity 32 (2015), 124008, arXiv:1410.5226v2
sources.locator: Read §4.1 What is a singularity?, §4.2 The key concept of closed trapped surface, Theorem 2 (Penrose singularity theorem), and its proof-strategy discussion on PDF pp. 9–10.

contents.name: §4.1 What is a singularity?
contents.support: Supports defining the theorem conclusion as geodesic incompleteness without claiming curvature misbehavior or a singular point in the manifold.

contents.name: §4.2 The key concept of closed trapped surface
contents.support: Supports the compact closed surface and two negative future expansion convention; the local definition strengthens this with patchwise null branches so no global normal frame is assumed.

contents.name: Theorem 2 (Penrose singularity theorem) and the compact-boundary/topological proof strategy
contents.support: Supports the theorem’s hypotheses and the compact horismos followed by a topological contradiction; all cited steps are locally proved from inspected suppliers.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete theorem statement and proof-strategy discussion, and the complete relevant portions of §§4.1–4.2.
source_review.supports: The distinction between incompleteness and curvature singularity, the definition of closed trapped surfaces, the standard Penrose hypotheses, and the compact-boundary/topological proof outline.
source_review.limitations: The review paper sketches the argument and its convergence condition; it is not used as a substitute for the complete local proofs. Its historical Einstein-equation presentation is not adopted as an extra premise.

sources.title: José Luis Jaramillo, Juan Antonio Valiente Kroon, and Éric Gourgoulhon, From Geometry to Numerics: Interdisciplinary Aspects in Mathematical and Numerical Relativity, arXiv:0712.2332v2 (2008)
sources.locator: Read §2.1 Asymptotic flatness, §2.2 Black holes, and §6.2.2 Seminal concepts and objects: trapped surfaces.

contents.name: §2.1 Asymptotic flatness and conformal completion
contents.support: Supports treating null infinity as part of supplied conformal asymptotic data rather than an automatic feature of any Lorentzian manifold.

contents.name: §2.2 Black holes
contents.support: Supports defining the black region as the complement of the causal past of future null infinity and its boundary as the event horizon, with the global qualifications stated.

contents.name: §6.2.2 Seminal concepts and objects: trapped surfaces
contents.support: Supports the two null expansions and the distinction between global event horizons and quasi-local trapped or marginal surfaces; the local definition fixes its own normalization and outward-direction data.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete relevant text in §§2.1–2.2 and §6.2.2.
source_review.supports: The asymptotic completion context for black-hole regions, the event-horizon definition, and trapped-surface/MOTS conventions.
source_review.limitations: This survey assumes orientability for globally selected null normal fields in its discussion and uses a different null-pair normalization. The local definition uses patchwise branches, the library normalization g(ell,k)=-2, and a supplied outward ray. The survey’s extra causal/global qualifications are not imported silently.
